before.zh: 汉之三年，项羽几番截断汉军甬道，荥阳城里的汉王断了粮，派人请和，条件是把荥阳以西割给汉。项羽本想答应，历阳侯范增拦住：「漢易與耳，今釋弗取，後必悔之。」——汉军眼下好打，放过了要后悔。楚军随即急围荥阳。
before.en: In the third year of Han, Xiang Yu cut the Han army's supply road several times. Trapped in Xingyang and out of food, the King of Han sent an offer to make peace, on condition that everything west of Xingyang be given to Han. Xiang Yu was ready to accept, but Fan Zeng of Liyang stopped him: "The Han army is easy to deal with; if you let them go now and do not take them, you will regret it later." The Chu forces then pressed the siege of Xingyang hard.

before.zh: 汉王缺的不是兵，是一个能让楚营自己散掉的缺口。刚从楚营来投的陈平接下了这件事。同一年里，项羽身边先后少了两个人：陈平投汉在前，亚父范增求去在后。两件事被写进同一条因果链，走的理由并不相同。
before.en: What the King of Han lacked was not men but a crack that would make the Chu camp fall apart on its own. Chen Ping, who had just come over from Chu, took the job. Within the same year Xiang Yu lost two people from his side: Chen Ping left for Han first, and his "Second Father" Fan Zeng asked to leave later. The two events are written into one chain of cause and effect, but the reasons for leaving were not the same.

after.zh: 汉之三年，项羽几番截断汉军甬道，荥阳城里的汉王断了粮，派人请和，条件是把荥阳以西割给汉。项羽本想答应，历阳侯范增拦住：「漢易與耳，今釋弗取，後必悔之。」——汉军眼下好打，放过了要后悔。楚军随即急围荥阳。
after.en: In the third year of Han, Xiang Yu cut the Han army's supply road several times. Trapped in Xingyang and out of food, the King of Han sent an offer to make peace, on condition that everything west of Xingyang be given to Han. Xiang Yu was ready to accept, but Fan Zeng of Liyang stopped him: "The Han army is easy to deal with; if you let them go now and do not take them, you will regret it later." The Chu forces then pressed the siege of Xingyang hard.

after.zh: 照《史记》的写法，汉王这一次没有硬拼，而是想办法让楚营自己生疑，出主意的是早先从项羽那边投奔过来的陈平。项羽身边先后少了两个人：先是陈平投汉，后是亚父范增求去。两人都说过「骸骨」二字，走的理由却不一样。
after.en: As the Records tell it, this time the King of Han did not try to fight his way out. He looked for a way to make the Chu camp turn on itself, and the plan came from Chen Ping, who had earlier crossed over from Xiang Yu's side. Xiang Yu lost two men in turn: first Chen Ping, who went over to Han, and later Fan Zeng, his "Second Father", who asked to go home. Both men used the same old phrase for resigning, asking for their "bones", but they left for different reasons.

reason: Removed unsupported '同一年' dating and '刚' (review issues hook[1], context[0]); framed 汉王's aim as the Records' account rather than his inner state; added the evidence-backed '请骸骨' echo.

before.zh: 时间是汉之三年，地点在荥阳，汉军被围、粮道断绝。项羽这边有被尊为亚父的范增，封历阳侯，另有钟离眛、龙且、周殷等将领——按陈平的说法，这样的骨干不过几人。汉王那边，陈平刚从楚营转投过来，此前先后跟过魏王、项王，眼下在汉营管护军，同僚有绛侯、灌婴等将领。
before.en: The time is the third year of Han; the place is Xingyang, where the Han army was besieged and its supply line cut. On Xiang Yu's side there was Fan Zeng, honoured as "Second Father" and enfeoffed as Marquis of Liyang, along with generals such as Zhongli Mo, Long Ju and Zhou Yin — by Chen Ping's own count, such key men were only a handful. On the King of Han's side, Chen Ping had just crossed over from the Chu camp. Before that he had served the King of Wei and then the King of Chu. Now he supervised the army in the Han camp, with generals such as the Marquis of Jiang and Guan Ying as colleagues.

after.zh: 时间是汉之三年（一般折算为公元前204年），地点在荥阳，汉军被围、粮道被断。项羽身边有被尊为“亚父”的历阳侯范增，还有钟离眛、龙且、周殷等将领——按陈平的说法，这样的骨干「不過數人耳」。汉王那边，陈平此前已从楚营投来，这时任护军中尉，监护诸将。
after.en: The time is the third year of Han (usually dated to 204 BC); the place is Xingyang, where the Han army was besieged and its supply road cut. Around Xiang Yu stood Fan Zeng, Lord of Liyang, whom he honoured as "Second Father", and generals such as Zhongli Mo, Long Ju and Zhou Yin. By Chen Ping's count, men of that calibre "were no more than a few". On the Han side, Chen Ping had defected from Chu some time earlier and now served as Commandant Protector of the Army, overseeing the generals.

reason: Removed '刚从楚营转投'; Chen Ping's post at the siege is 护军中尉 per A-E9 sequence; added standard BC year with 'usually dated'.

before.zh: 陈平的来路是一路换东家换出来的。他对汉王说过：魏王不能用他的计，才去事项王；项王「項王不能信人，其所任愛，非諸項即妻之昆弟」，信任全在本家和妻族手里，有奇士也用不上，于是离楚。来汉路上也不太平：渡河时船家见他一表人才独行，猜是逃将、腰里藏着金玉，动了杀心。他索性脱衣赤身帮着撑船——「解衣躶而佐刺船」——船家看清他身上没有东西，才停手。
before.en: Chen Ping's road to Han was made by changing masters. He told the King of Han that the King of Wei would not use his plans, so he went to serve the King of Chu; but the King of Chu "does not trust people — the ones he relies on and loves are none other than men of the Xiang clan or his wife's brothers", so even a man of rare talent had no chance, and he left Chu. The journey itself was rough too. When he crossed the river, the boatman saw a well-dressed man travelling alone, guessed he was a runaway general with gold and jade in his belt, and thought of killing him. Chen Ping simply stripped off and helped pole the boat, and only when the boatman saw he had nothing on him did he stop.

before.zh: 汉营里的麻烦换了形式。绛侯、灌婴等对汉王讲他坏话：人如冠玉，里子未必有；在家时「盜其嫂」；在魏在楚都待不住；如今管着护军，收将领的钱，钱多的得善处，钱少的得恶处。陈平不辩解往事，只承认自己空手来投，收下的钱多用作花用，不收就没有本钱办事（据《陈丞相世家》所记他的应答）。汉王的处理是向他致歉、厚加赏赐，拜为护军中尉，尽护诸将；诸将于是不敢再说。
before.en: In the Han camp the trouble took another form. The Marquis of Jiang, Guan Ying and others spoke ill of him to the King of Han: a fine-looking man, like a cap's jade ornament, but with nothing inside; at home he "had an affair with his sister-in-law"; he could not stay in Wei or in Chu; now he runs the supervision of the army and takes generals' money — those who pay more get good postings, those who pay less get bad ones. Chen Ping did not argue about his past. He only admitted that he came with nothing, that the money he took was mostly spent, and that without money he had no capital to get things done (according to his reply as recorded in the Hereditary House of Chancellor Chen). The King of Han's response was to apologise to him, reward him richly, and appoint him Commandant Protector of the Army over all the generals; the generals then dared not speak again.

before.zh: 陈平看楚营，看到一条缝：项王对人生疑、易信谗言，真正顶用的臣子不过几人。他请汉王拿出数万斤金行反间。汉王给了黄金四万斤，「恣所爲，不問其出入」。钱撒进楚军，流言跟着起来：钟离眛等人为项王领兵，「功多矣，然而終不得裂地而王」，如今想联合汉军灭项氏、分地称王。项羽果然不再信钟离眛等人。
before.en: Looking at the Chu camp, Chen Ping saw a crack: the King of Chu was suspicious of people and quick to believe slander, and the men who really mattered were only a few. He asked the King of Han to put up tens of thousands of catties of gold for a campaign of deception. The King of Han gave him forty thousand catties of gold, "to do with as he pleased, without asking what came in or went out". The money went into the Chu army, and rumours followed: Zhongli Mo and the others had won many victories commanding the King of Chu's troops, "yet were never given a share of land to become kings", and now they wanted to join Han, destroy the Xiang clan and split the land among themselves. Xiang Yu duly stopped trusting Zhongli Mo and the others.

before.zh: 最后是那一桌菜。项王派使者到汉营，汉王备下太牢具，端上来一见来人就装作吃惊：「吾以爲亞父使，乃項王使！」好菜撤下，换成粗劣的草具招待。使者回去照实回报，项王由此大疑亚父。范增主张急攻荥阳，项王不肯听。范增怒道：「天下事大定矣，君王自為之！願請骸骨歸！」项王答应了。他还没走到彭城，背上发疽而死。
before.en: Then came that meal. The King of Chu sent an envoy to the Han camp, and the King of Han prepared a full taolao feast and brought it up — but on seeing the visitor he pretended surprise: "I took you for an envoy of the Second Father, but you are an envoy of the King of Chu!" The good food was taken away and coarse fare was served instead. The envoy reported back honestly, and from then on Xiang Yu deeply suspected the Second Father. Fan Zeng pressed for a quick attack on Xingyang; Xiang Yu refused to listen. Fan Zeng said angrily: "The great affairs of the world are nearly settled — Your Majesty can handle them yourself! I beg leave to resign and return home!" Xiang Yu agreed. Before he reached Pengcheng, an ulcer broke out on his back and he died.

after.zh: 陈平投汉的路上就差点送命。渡河时，船家见他一表人才、独自赶路，猜他是逃亡的将领、腰里藏着金玉，起了杀心。他干脆脱掉衣服，赤身帮着撑船——「解衣躶而佐刺船」——船家看清他身上什么也没有，才作罢。
after.en: Chen Ping nearly died on his way to Han. Crossing a river alone, he looked to the boatman like a runaway officer with gold and jade hidden in his belt, and the man eyed him with murder in mind. Chen Ping took off his clothes and helped pole the boat. Once the boatman saw he had nothing on him, he left him alone.

after.zh: 到了汉营，麻烦换了形式。绛侯、灌婴等人在汉王面前说他坏话：长得好看，像帽子上的玉，里头未必有东西；在家时「盜其嫂」；在魏、在楚都待不住；如今管护军，还收将领们的钱，「金多者得善處，金少者得惡處」。汉王召他来责问，陈平答得很直白：魏王不用他的计，他才去投项王；项王「不能信人，其所任愛，非諸項即妻之昆弟」，有奇士也用不上，他才离开。至于收钱，「臣躶身來，不受金無以爲資」。他最后说，计策若没用，钱都还在，可以封好交公，「得請骸骨」——放他走。汉王于是道歉、厚赐，拜他为护军中尉，监护诸将；诸将不敢再说。
after.en: In the Han camp the danger took another form. The Marquis of Jiang, Guan Ying and others denounced him to the King of Han: handsome, like the jade on a cap, but perhaps hollow inside; at home he had had an affair with his sister-in-law; he had failed to settle with Wei or with Chu; and now, in charge of supervising the army, he took money from the generals, so that those who paid more got good posts and those who paid less got bad ones. The King of Han summoned him to explain. Chen Ping's answer was blunt. The King of Wei would not use his advice, so he went to Xiang Yu. Xiang Yu "cannot trust people; those he relies on and loves are all Xiangs or his wife's brothers", so even a man of rare talent was wasted, and he left. As for the money: "I came here naked. Without taking gold I had nothing to work with." If his plans were useless, he said, the gold was still there to be sealed and handed in, and he could ask for his bones, that is, be allowed to go. The King of Han apologised, rewarded him richly and made him Commandant Protector over all the generals. The generals said no more.

after.zh: 陈平看楚营，看到的是一条缝：项王「意忌信讒」，真正撑得住的骨干不过几人。他请汉王拿出几万斤金行反间。汉王给了黄金四万斤，「恣所爲，不問其出入」——随他怎么花，不过问去向。钱撒进楚军，流言跟着起来：钟离眛等人替项王打仗，「功多矣，然而終不得裂地而王」，要和汉联手灭项氏、分地称王。项羽果然对钟离眛等人起了疑心。
after.en: Looking at the Chu camp, Chen Ping saw a crack: Xiang Yu was "jealous and suspicious, and believed slander", and the men who truly held his side together were few. He asked for tens of thousands of catties of gold to sow discord. The King of Han handed over forty thousand catties, "to use as he pleased, without asking where it went". The money went into the Chu army, and so did a rumour: Zhongli Mo and others had won great merit for Xiang Yu "yet would never be given land to rule as kings", so they meant to join Han, destroy the Xiang clan and divide its lands. Xiang Yu did indeed begin to doubt Zhongli Mo and the others.

after.zh: 最后是那一桌菜。项王派使者到汉营，汉王备下牛羊猪俱全的太牢，端上来，一见来人便装作吃惊：「吾以爲亞父使，乃項王使！」好菜撤下，换上粗劣的饭食。使者回去照实禀报，项王于是大疑亚父。范增主张急攻荥阳，项王不肯听。范增听说自己被疑，怒道：「天下事大定矣，君王自爲之！願請骸骨歸！」《项羽本纪》说项王「許之」。他还没走到彭城，背上发疽而死。
after.en: Then came the meal. When Xiang Yu sent an envoy to the Han camp, the King of Han had a full feast of beef, mutton and pork brought in. Then, on seeing the man, he pretended to be startled: "I thought you were the Second Father's envoy, but you are Xiang Yu's!" The fine dishes were carried out and coarse food served instead. The envoy reported all of it, and Xiang Yu came to suspect the Second Father deeply. Fan Zeng urged a quick assault on Xingyang; Xiang Yu would not listen. Hearing that he was suspected, Fan Zeng said in anger: "The affairs of the realm are largely settled. Let Your Majesty manage them yourself! I ask for my bones, to go home!" The Basic Annals of Xiang Yu record that Xiang Yu "granted it". Before Fan Zeng reached Pengcheng, an abscess broke out on his back and he died.

reason: Restructured: boat episode first; Chen Ping's reply now quoted from extended A-E1 instead of the invented '钱多用作花用'; 不再信 -> 起了疑心; added 項羽本紀 '許之' attribution; English: dropped untranslated 'taolao', used Xiang Yu consistently.

before.zh: 两个人走的都绕着同一个字：信。陈平说项王不能信人，赏赐与职位绕着本家、妻族转，外来人进不了圈；范增是老臣，一旦被疑，连急攻荥阳的话都没人听。一种解释是（作者推断）：反间计咬得住，是因为流言踩中了真实的痛处。陈平自己分析过项王：待人「恭敬愛人」，礼数不缺，可是「行功爵邑，重之」，封赏看得很紧，所以士人来归者多、愿附从者少。流言说的恰是功高而不得封地，像把火星丢进堆好的柴。至于项羽为何就此信了，史书没有细讲。
before.en: Both men left over the same word: trust. Chen Ping said the King of Chu could not trust people, that rewards and posts went round the family and the wife's kin, and outsiders could not get inside the circle. Fan Zeng was a veteran, yet once he fell under suspicion, even his advice to attack Xingyang fast was ignored. One explanation (the author's own inference) is that the deception bit because the rumour landed on a real sore point. Chen Ping himself had analysed the King of Chu: towards people he was "respectful and caring", never short of courtesy, but "as for rewarding merit with ranks and fiefs, he held them dear" — he was tight with grants — so many scholars came to him but few stayed attached. The rumour said exactly that: men of great merit got no land, like a spark dropped into stacked firewood. As for why Xiang Yu believed it, the histories do not go into detail.

before.zh: 还可以多留一个心眼（作者提出）：太牢与恶草具那一幕太像剧本，它也许实有其事，也许经过叙事整理，仅凭现有材料无法判断。它能确定的作用只有一个——让人看见疑心是怎样被一口一口喂大的。
before.en: One more caution (the author's): the scene with the fine feast and the coarse fare is too much like a script. It may have happened as told, or it may have been tidied up in the telling; on the material we have, there is no way to judge. It establishes only one thing — it shows how suspicion is fed, one mouthful at a time.

after.zh: 两个人离开，都绕着同一个字：信。陈平说项王的信任只给项家人和妻族；范增是老臣，一旦被疑，连急攻荥阳的主张也没人听。陈平对项王还有一段更细的分析：项王「恭敬愛人」，所以「士之廉節好禮者多歸之」；可是「至於行功爵邑，重之」，舍不得封赏，于是另一些人「亦以此不附」。一种解释是（作者推断）：反间计咬得住，是因为流言说的正是“功多而不得封王”，踩中了楚营里本就存在的不满。至于项羽为什么就这样信了，史书没有细讲。
after.en: Both departures turn on one word: trust. Chen Ping said Xiang Yu's trust went only to his own clan and his wife's family; Fan Zeng was a senior adviser, yet once suspected, even his advice to storm Xingyang was ignored. Chen Ping had also given a finer reading of Xiang Yu: he was "respectful and kind to people", so "men of integrity who valued courtesy flocked to him"; but "when it came to granting ranks and fiefs for merit, he held on to them", so others "for this reason did not stay attached". One explanation, and it is the author's inference, is that the plot worked because the rumour named a real grievance: great merit, no land. Why Xiang Yu believed it so readily, the histories do not say.

after.zh: 还有一处值得留意（作者提出）：陈平和范增都说过“请骸骨”。陈平说「得請骸骨」，是把去留交给汉王判断，结果被留下、被重用；范增说「願請骸骨歸」，是在被疑之后负气求去，项王也就放他走了。同样几个字，一次用来换取信任，一次说在信任破裂之后。至于太牢与粗食那一幕，情节太像戏，可能实有其事，也可能经过叙事加工，现有材料无法判断。
after.en: One more thing worth noticing, and this is the author's observation: both men used the phrase "ask for my bones". Chen Ping said it to put the decision in the king's hands, and he was kept and promoted. Fan Zeng said it in anger after he had been suspected, and Xiang Yu let him go. The same words, once to earn trust and once after trust was gone. As for the scene of the feast and the coarse food, it reads like theatre; it may have happened as told or been polished in the telling, and the surviving material cannot settle which.

reason: Fixed the misreading that merged two groups of 士 (review analysis[0]); added the documented echo between 陈平's and 范增's '请骸骨' as a marked author observation.

before.zh: 五个人的产品小组年底发项目奖金，组长的方案是按入职年限排。贡献最大的是半年前才进来的后端，有人替他不平，也有人说规矩就是规矩。可以先做一件小事：发钱前把各人这半年的产出列成一张表，先定口径，再定数字。分配不必人人一样，但要经得起复述。
before.en: A five-person product team is splitting a year-end project bonus. The team lead's plan ranks people by length of service. The person who contributed most is a backend developer who joined only six months ago. Some say this is unfair to him; others say rules are rules. One small step can come first: before the money goes out, list everyone's output over the past six months in a single table. Agree on the measure before you agree on the numbers. The split need not be equal, but it should survive being explained.

before.zh: 一个外包转正的同事接手采购，老同事私下嘀咕他会让熟人的供应商沾光。他没赌咒发誓，只把三家比价的记录发进群里，每笔差价写明理由，谁都能翻。外来者要化掉怀疑，最省力的不是表态，是把过程摊开让人看。
before.en: A colleague who moved from contractor to permanent staff takes over purchasing, and older hands mutter privately that he will favour suppliers he knows. He does not swear oaths; he just posts the three-way price comparison into the group chat and gives a reason for every price difference, open for anyone to check. For an outsider to dissolve suspicion, the cheapest move is not to make statements but to lay the process open for people to see.

after.zh: 一个小组里传出话：某位骨干拿了别家的邀约，快要走了。负责人第一反应是去查谁在传话。更有用的第一个问题可能是：如果这话是真的，她为什么会想走？传言有人信，往往是因为它说中了一件大家心里都知道、却没人摆上桌面的事，比如一拖再拖的晋升。先处理那件事，传言就没那么有力了。
after.en: Word goes round a small team that a key member has an offer elsewhere and is about to leave. The manager's first impulse is to find out who started the talk. A more useful first question may be: if it were true, why would she want to go? A rumour spreads when it names something everyone already knows but nobody has raised, such as a promotion that keeps getting postponed. Deal with that, and the rumour loses most of its power.

He does not swear oaths; he just posts the three-way price comparison into the group chat and gives a reason for every price difference, open for anyone to check. before.en: Spending those forty thousand catties of gold with not even a ledger would be an internal-control failure today, not generosity. Chen Ping's move was a split-the-enemy operation: what the money bought was other people's mistrust, not cooperation. Staying on to clear things up, or starting fresh somewhere else, are both possibilities the author raises; there is no need to copy his storming off.
